discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind admission of the eight Pi/OpenCode harness-by-model cells from the committed OpenBench M4 matrix. Each model pair shares the same three benchmark tasks and three trials per task. W1 preserves the source-reported nine-cell mean objective score and source timing/token telemetry without cleaning failure rows, changing denominators, or reproducing source ordering claims.

provenance_strength.w1_treatment: admitted from the historical M4 publication commit with all eight harness-by-model cells preserved; documented adapter exceptions remain in the source nine-cell result surface and are not silently removed

protocol_deviations_and_failures.detail: The first long-lived background run was externally reaped after 43 of 72 real cells. The benchmark resumed by run_id and skipped completed cells; the source reports no lost rows.

A historical OpenCode adapter timeout handler attempted bytes-plus-string concatenation. The committed rows retain these exceptions with completed=false and score 0: seven GLM-4.7-Flash OpenCode cells and one Kimi OpenCode cell.

non_admission_dispositions.reason: Published routing measurements intentionally generalize lane/model identities and remove raw private inputs, so the exercised systems cannot be pinned without inventing historical identity.

The committed fallback leaderboard contains concrete qwen3:8b agent-only rows, but those runs predate the first public BenchLoop CLI commit; W1 did not back-project later implementation code onto the historical rows.

The repository fixes model/gateway and publishes the benchmark scaffold, while scored hidden-suite outcomes remain on the grading service/instructor side and no immutable committed result surface was located.

The repository publishes a controlled four-configuration same-model benchmark and aggregate tables, but raw run JSON and full traces are gitignored. It remains a candidate for a separate weaker-evidence pass rather than being conflated with OpenBench M4's committed per-cell data.
